name: dyed-flax-fibres-georgia
description: Hunter-gatherers in a Caucasus cave twisted and dyed wild flax fibres, the oldest known cloth-making thread.

name: silk-weaving-china-legend
description: Legend credits an empress with unravelling a silkworm cocoon, starting the making of the world's most prized fabric.

name: victoria-white-wedding-gown
description: A young British queen chose white satin for her wedding, starting the fashion for white bridal dresses.

name: worth-paris-couture-house
friendly_name: Worth Opens a Paris Couture House
description: An English tailor in Paris designed seasonal collections shown on live models, founding haute couture.

name: burberry-gabardine
description: A draper developed a tightly woven, weatherproof cotton twill that became the basis of the trench coat.

name: viscose-rayon-patented
description: British chemists patented a way to turn wood pulp into a silky fibre, the first widely made artificial fabric.

name: lacoste-polo-shirt
description: A tennis star put a crocodile on a breathable cotton piqué shirt and began selling it to the public.

name: hepburn-givenchy-black-dress
description: A long black evening gown and pearls in a film about breakfast at a jeweller became an icon of style.

name: monroe-sheer-birthday-dress
description: A skin-tight, crystal-covered gown was worn to sing for a president, then sold for millions decades later.

name: von-furstenberg-wrap-dress
description: A jersey dress that tied at the waist became a symbol of women's independence in the workplace.

name: diana-revenge-dress
description: A royal wore a daring, off-the-shoulder black dress to a gala on the night a rival story broke.

name: jlo-green-versace-dress
description: A plunging silk chiffon gown at a music awards show was so popular it inspired the creation of image search.

name: lady-gaga-meat-dress
description: A pop star arrived at a music awards ceremony wearing a dress made of raw beef, sparking global debate.
